text:
In Angostura, the river

becomes thin and deep like a secret,

it has the intensity of an idea

that puts the wrinkle on the Middle Rock.


In Angostura, the water

has the depth of a concept,

and perhaps here the river is Bolívar's shadow,

metaphor for a soul that cannot fit inside the body.


See how it comes downstream;

think something in the river without fences or ports,

broad as far as the horizon,

hot as the Desert.

The boat is an instant in the life of water,

a leaf on a tree, a note in thunder,

and in the boat came the hope of America,

a mere sip of a man, a feather in flight,

the first drop where there is born

the Orinoco of Dream.

And it arrived here, at Angostura, on a primitive beach;

the canoe moored; see him sink into the ground

the fine heel, with the sting

of the wasp that wants to know its hive;

follow him, climbing the slope

toward the city; a flutter

of bells announces his arrival, the houses

don their Sunday clothes of flags and signs,

from Soledad canoes arrive with women

like baskets of mangoes and mereyes in season.

Angostura struts its jaunty elegance

to please the handsome Hero with black eyes.


And when he climbed the stairway

toward the summit of the Congress,

and when he turned back toward the beach

with the Republic in his chest,

what was that light, Orinoco,

that ruffled your muscles and bristled your nerves

and shook your deep fibers

from the foot of Maipures to the fist of Macareo?

Was it not the Homeland? Was it not the Homeland itself?

The age-old homeland born in your womb

and destined to live through the centuries, eternal as the World,

because if one day it dies within us, you will return from the Ocean.

translation.title: Angostura
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves Angostura, Bolívar, Maipures, Macareo, and the river-as-Homeland metaphor.
